name: Integrated WTI Forecast
point_meaning: Price median of the final calibrated predictive distribution.

delivery_scope.parameter_policy: Coefficients, preprocessing, weights and risk calibration frozen as of 2026-09-30.
delivery_scope.input_policy: Update each daily origin using only observations available under the existing publication rules.
delivery_scope.selection_policy: Pre-October historical development only. No October ranking, tuning or fallback selection.
delivery_scope.evidence_status: Previously inspected outcomes are not a fresh blind test; they cannot select candidates, parameters, upgrades or fallbacks.

module_roles.m1: Actual VECM forecasts enter the inherited residual system and the new convex family pool.
module_roles.m2: Actual monthly STL forecasts enter inherited residual models; long-history models add calendar and state interactions.
module_roles.lstm: Actual three-seed LSTM forecasts enter inherited residual models and the new family pool.
module_roles.ml_point: Existing point ML plus 2012-onward Ridge, Elastic Net, LightGBM and Huber residual candidates.
module_roles.ml_distribution: Selected ML conditional scale/shape plus historical fused-error calibration; 63 monotone quantiles preserve the point median.
module_roles.futures: Causal raw CL=F Close with a two-federal-business-day lag, also reported as a separate benchmark.

historical_inference.interpretation: Paired origin-level block bootstrap, blocks 20 and 60; conditional exploratory historical evidence.
historical_inference.source_limits: Same two-federal-business-day futures lag and current-vintage/publication assumptions as v3; base specifications condition the historical evaluation.

promotion_gate.rule: Later-history aggregate must improve over v3, and no horizon may degrade by more than 2%; no October ranking.

source_audit.availability: Session quote + 2 US federal business days; never same-day OHLCV.
source_audit.limitation: Current-vintage unadjusted Close; verified overlap through EIA historical endpoint, not a complete point-in-time vendor archive.

limitations: Same two-federal-business-day futures lag and current-vintage/publication assumptions as v3; base specifications condition the historical evaluation.
Previously inspected outcomes are not a fresh blind test; they cannot select candidates, parameters, upgrades or fallbacks.
Guard and asymmetric-tail research amendments followed inspection of pre-October historical results; this is adaptive development.
The 2.47% historical aggregate gain over v3 is not statistically significant; its 95% improvement interval is -3.54% to +5.73%.
The primary historical score is 0.46% worse than lagged-futures carry, although better than published-spot RW.
Forward risk coverage remains below 90% for every horizon; h5 coverage fell from 83.7% to 72.6%.
Forward h60 CRPS improved 20.0% vs v3 but remains 5.6% worse than historical simulation.
October has only 17/13 realized outcomes at h1/h5, and none at h20/h60; October h1/h5 do not beat v2.
Local member-input sensitivity proves model use, not beneficial out-of-sample contribution of each member.
Current-vintage data and full-window base-specification selection prevent a claim of a fully nested point-in-time blind test.
